rates.tr: Enflasyonu düşürmek için faiz yükselten ülkelerde ekonomik durgunluk yaşandı.
rates.en: Countries that raised interest rates to bring inflation down went through an economic slowdown.

sugar.tr: Şeker vergisi koyan ülkelerde gazlı içecek tüketimi düştü.
sugar.en: In countries that introduced a sugar tax, consumption of fizzy drinks fell.

wage.en: Raising the minimum wage did not reduce employment.

cases.label: ECB 1 strength of demand
cases.text: Furthermore, the strength of the economy is relevant to the risk of inflation pressures broadening beyond the initial shock: the stronger aggregate demand, the more scope firms have to pass higher input costs on to consumer prices.

cases.label: ECB 1 anchored expectations
cases.text: As long as expectations are firmly anchored and backed up by a track record of delivering on the inflation target, monetary policy can tolerate a more gradual return of inflation to target. But when expectations show signs of becoming less firmly anchored, a more forceful response may be required to prevent temporary shocks from becoming more persistent.

cases.label: ECB 1 underlying inflation
cases.text: Monetary policy needs to focus on underlying inflation to assess price stability. Although the ECB's inflation target is expressed in terms of headline inflation, the best way to achieve that target sustainably is, in many circumstances, to focus on the dynamics of underlying inflation.

cases.label: ECB 1 real rates
cases.text: In recent years, real interest rates at distant horizons have increased. This is happening at a time when the global economy is facing substantial demand for funding from both the public and private sectors, as fiscal deficits remain elevated across many countries and the AI buildout advances.

cases.label: ECB 1 what the ECB is doing
cases.text: This is what the ECB is doing. Faced with a renewed deterioration in the inflation outlook, we adjusted policy rates in a timely manner to limit the pass-through to underlying inflation and bring inflation back to target.

cases.label: banks capital
cases.text: On the contrary, they found that higher levels of capital lower both interest rate expenses and the volatility of earnings. This allows banks to reduce their funding premia, which drives up profitability.

cases.label: banks efficiency
cases.text: Together, these measures will facilitate a more efficient financial system. This will also allow a better channelling of funds into productive investments within the continent. Overall, it will make the EU economy more competitive.

cases.label: Sri Lanka literacy
cases.text: Financial literacy helps people interpret these conditions accurately. People need to understand how inflation affects the real value of income and the affordability of financial commitments. They also need to distinguish between the price level and the inflation. Slower price increases do not mean lower prices.

cases.label: Philippines money supply
cases.text: So when you want to lower inflation, you tighten money supply, you reduce money supply. But in the 1990s, we found out that it works the same way if you raise interest rates. Tightening money supply is the same as raising interest rates.

cases.label: Philippines target
cases.text: By the way, 3 percent is our target for inflation. That, we figured out, is the sweet spot for a growing economy like ours. Other central banks, the US has a 2 percent target. Other developed countries have 2 percent targets.

cases.label: ECB 5 diagnosis
cases.text: A collection of other driving forces (fiscal policy, AI and financial conditions) are also shaping output and inflation dynamics in the euro area, both directly and via their interactions with the energy supply shock. This means that the appropriate monetary policy should not be interpreted as solely driven by the energy supply shock but rather requires a multi-pronged diagnostic assessment.

cases.label: Norway wages
cases.text: First, the global price shock that hit the economy in the aftermath of the pandemic made imports more expensive. But it also raised the prices of Norway's exports. Higher export prices contributed to stronger wage growth, which is now sustaining inflation.

cases.label: Africa payments
cases.text: Enhancing cross-border payments is thus a necessity for the resilience and economic transformation of African economies. But it is not sufficient.

cases.label: ECB 1 restraining demand
cases.text: By restraining growth in aggregate demand, higher interest rates can limit the extent to which a relative price shock, often originating from the energy sector, can broaden into more persistent, economy-wide inflation.

cases.label: ECB 1 larger decline avoided
cases.text: Instead, the trade-off between inflation and output that arises under an adverse supply shock is resolved by allowing inflation to return to target more gradually in exchange for avoiding a larger decline in economic activity.

cases.label: ECB 1 GDP may respond more
cases.text: Some models imply stronger transmission than the elasticities used in the staff projections, especially with respect to the impact on GDP. It is therefore possible that the economy responds more to the recent tightening than currently assumed, which would dampen medium-term inflationary pressures compared with the baseline projection.

cases.label: ECB 1 credit still robust
cases.text: In any case, the recent robust credit dynamics suggest that financial conditions are not yet restrictive or that parts of lending, particularly related to AI investment, have become less sensitive to interest rates as expected returns have risen.

cases.label: sugar Denmark
cases.text: Denmark's tax on soft drinks had no measurable effect on consumption: sales of carbonated soft drinks did not fall after the tax was raised, because consumers bought the same drinks cheaply across the German border.

cases.label: rates in other words
cases.text: The monetary tightening of 2022 pushed borrowing costs up sharply. Consumer prices stopped climbing, but the economy slipped into a downturn, with output falling for three quarters.

cases.label: rates plain
cases.text: After the central bank raised its policy rate from 0.25% to 5.25% to bring inflation down, output contracted for two consecutive quarters and the economy entered a recession.

cases.label: sugar Mexico
cases.text: In Mexico, purchases of taxed sugar-sweetened beverages declined by 6% in the first year after the excise tax was introduced in 2014, and by 9.7% in the second year, compared with the trend expected without the tax.

cases.label: wage Seattle
cases.text: After Seattle raised its minimum wage to 13 dollars, hours worked in low-wage jobs fell by around 9 percent, and the number of such jobs declined, according to the city's evaluation.

cases.label: wage 138 increases
cases.text: Across the 138 increases studied, the number of low-wage jobs remained essentially unchanged five years after the minimum wage was raised, while the earnings of affected workers rose.

cases.label: words only
cases.text: Interest rates on savings accounts rose last year, so savers earned more on their deposits. A recession in the local housing market was blamed on the inflation of building costs.

cases.label: Norway close
cases.text: Part of the explanation lies in the weight the committee has given to striking an appropriate balance between reducing inflation and sustaining employment. More aggressive monetary tightening would have brought inflation down faster.

cases.label: ECB 1 view it rejects
cases.before: It is often argued that inflation targeting implies that central banks should look through adverse supply shocks that push up inflation and weaken output.
cases.text: The reason given is that monetary policy cannot address the source of the shock. Higher interest rates, for example, will not remove supply disruptions or reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Tightening would therefore unnecessarily weaken the economy without eliminating the underlying cause of higher inflation, which will eventually vanish by itself.
cases.after: This characterisation, however, is too simple. In the benchmark models underlying modern monetary policy frameworks, the distinction between supply and demand shocks does not alter the direction of the optimal policy response.
